children: Nigel Farage said Reform UK was "ready to form a government" after securing another £36m donation from billionaire Christopher Harborne, matching a similar contribution announced a day earlier from crypto entrepreneur Ben Delo,
The Telegraph

reported. The paper said the two gifts bring Reform's total fundraising this year to more than £86m, far exceeding the sums raised by the Conservatives and Labour. Farage has reportedly received a personal boost after a difficult summer, with the influx of cash expected to accelerate the party's efforts to build a nationwide campaign machine ahead of the next general election.
Britain's air‑traffic control system could become "unfixable" if it suffers a major failure from 2030 onwards,
The Times
reported, citing concerns inside
Nats

. According to the paper, the core processor that manages all aircraft entering UK airspace will be "unsupported" from 2030, raising fears that any breakdown could lead to days‑long paralysis. One Nats source likened the situation to owning equipment whose manufacturer "is no longer around", leaving no parts or expertise available if something goes wrong. The report comes as Nats chief executive Martin Rolfe faces pressure after a third IT outage in three years. Rolfe must present initial findings this week to regulators following Tuesday's four‑hour system failure that caused widespread disruption at UK airports.
Jaguar Land Rover

was said to be preparing to enter the US pick‑up truck market for the first time with an American version of its Defender model, The Times reported. The paper said the UK carmaker was expected to unveil the plans within months as chief executive PB Balaji seeks to revive momentum after cutting 4,000 jobs. The Defender pick‑up will be built in the US through a new joint venture with
Stellantis
, owner of Ram - the third‑largest pick‑up brand in America. The move marks a significant strategic shift for JLR as it targets a slice of the $80bn US pick‑up segment.
Anthropic
chief executive Dario Amodei has urged the AI industry to "slow down", outlining a three‑part plan to improve oversight and safety,
The Guardian

reported. In a social‑media post, Amodei linked to an essay titled We Must Pace the Frontier, pledging that Anthropic would give independent evaluators permanent, employee‑level access to its systems to verify safety compliance and monitor incidents. The appeal followed claims from former Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon, who warned last week that AI could cause human extinction by 2030. Coxon said he resigned because Anthropic and OpenAI were "racing straight to self‑improving superintelligence", arguing that neither company was acting responsibly.
Tesco
has contacted City of London Police after its branding was used without permission in online adverts for unlicensed casinos,
The Guardian
reported. According to the paper, the supermarket was among several major UK businesses - alongside
Barclays
and sports stars including Lewis Hamilton - whose images have been misused by offshore gambling operators seeking to exploit brand recognition. The ads, promoted via
Meta

platforms such as Facebook and Instagram, falsely implied that the companies had launched their own casino services. Tesco said it was taking action to stop the misuse of its name and protect customers from fraudulent promotions.
Reporting by Iain Gilbert at Sharecast.com
